channel.title: Mastering Epistemology (audiobook)
channel.description: The narrated edition of Mastering Epistemology, a free, complete guide to knowledge, evidence and critical thinking: sixteen chapters, each ending with a spoken quiz. Narrated with a synthetic voice.
channel.itunes:author: Mastering Epistemology
channel.itunes:summary: The narrated edition of Mastering Epistemology, a free, complete guide to knowledge, evidence and critical thinking: sixteen chapters, each ending with a spoken quiz. Narrated with a synthetic voice.

item.title: Chapter 1: What Is Epistemology?
item.itunes:title: What Is Epistemology?
item.description: The central questions; three kinds of knowing; belief, credence, and acceptance; the a priori, analytic, and necessary; epistemic versus practical reasons; the map of the field Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/01-what-is-epistemology.html

item.title: Chapter 2: A History of the Theory of Knowledge
item.itunes:title: A History of the Theory of Knowledge
item.description: From the Presocratics, Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle through Indian, Islamic, and Chinese traditions, Descartes, Locke, Hume, Reid, and Kant, to pragmatism, Popper, Wittgenstein, Quine, and Gettier Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/02-history-of-epistemology.html

item.title: Chapter 3: Logic and the Anatomy of Arguments
item.itunes:title: Logic and the Anatomy of Arguments
item.description: Deduction, induction, and abduction; validity and soundness; conditionals and necessary/sufficient conditions; valid forms and formal fallacies; hidden premises; charity; argument mapping; the Toulmin model Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/03-logic-and-arguments.html

item.title: Chapter 4: Language, Concepts, and Definitions
item.itunes:title: Language, Concepts, and Definitions
item.description: Sense and reference; kinds of definition; ambiguity and vagueness; verbal disputes; loaded language and framing; contested concepts; the is–ought gap; thought experiments; reflective equilibrium Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/04-language-concepts-and-definitions.html

item.title: Chapter 5: What Is Knowledge?
item.itunes:title: What Is Knowledge?
item.description: Justified true belief; the Gettier problem; reliabilism, sensitivity, safety, virtue, and knowledge-first theories; epistemic luck; the value of knowledge; understanding and wisdom Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/05-the-nature-of-knowledge.html

item.title: Chapter 6: Justification: The Structure of Good Reasons
item.itunes:title: Justification: The Structure of Good Reasons
item.description: Defeaters; the regress problem; foundationalism, coherentism, infinitism, and their hybrids; internalism versus externalism; evidentialism; the problem of the criterion; fallibilism Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/06-justification.html

item.title: Chapter 7: The Sources of Knowledge
item.itunes:title: The Sources of Knowledge
item.description: Perception, memory, introspection, reason, and testimony: how each works and how each fails; knowledge by presence; when to trust intuition Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/07-sources-of-knowledge.html

item.title: Chapter 8: Skepticism and Its Answers
item.itunes:title: Skepticism and Its Answers
item.description: Pyrrhonian and Cartesian skepticism; the brain in a vat; the closure argument; Moore, contextualism, hinge epistemology, and other responses; healthy versus corrosive skepticism Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/08-skepticism.html

item.title: Chapter 9: Induction, Probability, and Bayesian Reasoning
item.itunes:title: Induction, Probability, and Bayesian Reasoning
item.description: Hume’s problem; grue and the ravens; probability; Bayes’ theorem with worked examples; base rates, the conjunction fallacy, Monty Hall, regression to the mean, Simpson’s paradox; calibration; p-values and risk Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/09-induction-probability-bayes.html

item.title: Chapter 10: Science, Evidence, and Explanation
item.itunes:title: Science, Evidence, and Explanation
item.description: Falsifiability; Duhem–Quine; Kuhn and Lakatos; inference to the best explanation; realism; causation, correlation, and randomized trials; values in science; consensus; the replication crisis; spotting pseudoscience Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/10-science-and-evidence.html

item.title: Chapter 11: Truth, Relativism, and Objectivity
item.itunes:title: Truth, Relativism, and Objectivity
item.description: Theories of truth; the liar paradox; relativism and its critics; social construction; objectivity and perspective; post-truth and bullshit Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/11-truth-and-relativism.html

item.title: Chapter 12: Social Epistemology: Knowing Together
item.itunes:title: Social Epistemology: Knowing Together
item.description: Trust and expertise; choosing between experts; peer disagreement; epistemic injustice; standpoint theory; echo chambers; cascades and crowds; misinformation, propaganda, and conspiracy theories; institutions; AI Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/12-social-epistemology.html

item.title: Chapter 13: Intellectual Virtue and the Ethics of Belief
item.itunes:title: Intellectual Virtue and the Ethics of Belief
item.description: Clifford versus James; intellectual virtues and vices; humility and open-mindedness; pragmatic and moral encroachment; faith, reason, and religious epistemology Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/13-virtues-and-ethics-of-belief.html

item.title: Chapter 14: The Psychology of Reasoning: How Minds Actually Work
item.itunes:title: The Psychology of Reasoning: How Minds Actually Work
item.description: Dual-process theories; heuristics and biases; confirmation and myside bias; motivated reasoning; overconfidence; identity-protective cognition; the argumentative theory; what debiasing works; superforecasting Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/14-psychology-of-reasoning.html

item.title: Chapter 15: A Field Guide to Fallacies
item.itunes:title: A Field Guide to Fallacies
item.description: More than forty fallacies and rhetorical tactics, each with examples, its legitimate cousin, and how to respond; practice exercises Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/15-fallacies.html

item.title: Chapter 16: The Critical Thinker's Toolkit: Analyzing Discussions and Framing Arguments
item.itunes:title: The Critical Thinker's Toolkit: Analyzing Discussions and Framing Arguments
item.description: A seven-step method for analyzing any discussion; stasis theory; finding the crux; framing your own arguments; burden of proof; razors; the ethics of discussion; five worked case studies; checklists Read the chapter: https://epis.duckdns.org/guide/16-critical-thinking-toolkit.html
